The FV Flowplayer Video Player plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[videos][0][fv_wp_flowplayer_field_src]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.5.57.7212 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The fv_player_db_save AJAX endpoint's INSERT path is gated only by a per-user preview nonce and never calls current_user_can(), allowing any authenticated subscriber-level user who possesses their own nonce to store the malicious payload. Exploitation by attackers with subscriber-level access and above requires that administrator has enabled the plugin option fvwpflowplayer['profile_videos_enable_bio']=true (off by default), which enqueues the shortcode editor and the per-user preview_nonce on wp-admin/profile.php for every logged-in user. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

RabbitMQ is a messaging and streaming broker. In the affected revision identified by the advisory, the AMQP 1.0 server_mode parser in deps/amqp10_common/src/amqp10_binary_parser.erl stops at the first body section and preserves the remaining bytes in bare_and_footer without validating message-section order. An authenticated publisher with write permission can place a properties section carrying a forged user-id after the body, causing rabbit_access_control:check_user_id/2 to see no user-id while permissive downstream AMQP 1.0 decoders or AMQP 0-9-1 conversion through classic and quorum queues expose the forged identity. Applications that rely on RabbitMQ-validated user-id metadata can therefore accept attacker-controlled publisher attribution. Strict consumers that reject out-of-order sections are not vulnerable to identity spoofing, and the issue does not bypass broker routing or destination authorization. This issue is fixed in version 4.3.5.

Issue summary: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX
may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end
of the caller-supplied output buffer.

Impact summary: No path by which an attacker can trigger this has been
identified. An application that passes an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock() could suffer a heap buffer overflow, crashing or corrupting
its own memory, but it must itself supply such a length.

CWE: CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound

Description: EVP_EncodeBlock() base64-encodes a buffer of a caller-supplied
length into an output buffer that the caller allocates. The caller is expected
to reserve 4*((len+2)/3)+1 bytes. For input lengths close to INT_MAX, the
arithmetic that computes the encoded length overflows a signed integer, so the
function writes more data than the documented output size. The result is a
heap buffer overflow in the calling process.

Reaching this requires an application to pass an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock(). OpenSSL's TLS, QUIC and CMS implementations never encode
buffers of that size, and the command line tools cannot practically be made to
do so: the limits on reading a proxy password from a file and on bignum sizes
prevent it. An application that accepts an attacker-controlled length and
forwards it to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own bound check is exposed.

The severity is Low because no attacker-controlled path to the overflow is
known. The caller must already hold a buffer of about two gigabytes before the
defect can be reached.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event_street' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has granted the mc_add_events capability to Subscriber-level users via the plugin's Permissions settings; once granted, the Subscriber can store the payload without the mc_edit_locations capability because mc_admin_save() does not enforce it before calling mc_insert_location().

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could modify a search macro associated with risk exclusions. Scheduled Risk data model acceleration searches could later run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands from that macro with elevated permissions. With this access, the user who modified the search macro could expose stored credentials and modify indexes or lookup data available to those searches.
The vulnerability is possible because the Splunk Enterprise Security app metadata grants the "ess_analyst" role write access to the risk exclusion search macro.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security), Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.3/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security), and Use search macros in searches (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.4/search-macros/use-search-macros-in-searches) in the Splunk documentation.

The Nexter Extension – Security, Performance, Code Snippets & Site Toolkit plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 This is due to the role_switcher_to_view_admin_as() function handling the `reset-view` branch without a capability check or nonce when the caller's own login is supplied, combined with an incomplete cleanup hook (maybe_prevent_switchback_to_administrator) that exits early when the user's current roles equal the stored view role and that is never triggered when WordPress core's WP_User::set_role() short-circuits because the account already has only the target role. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to elevate their privileges to Administrator.
vp: nexter extension – security, performance, code snippets & site toolkit

A nonce sufficient to pass the initial nonce check is publicly exposed on any board listing page, meaning no prior authentication or privileged access is required to initiate the exploit.

The Seraphinite Accelerator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.31 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has previously enabled the 'Enable logging' and 'HTTP trace' diagnostic options in the plugin's Advanced → Debug settings, both of which are disabled by default.

The Simple Membership WP user Import plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.2 This is due to missing or incorrect nonce validation on the add function. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to import arbitrary WordPress users into Simple Membership and modify their WordPress role via the plugin's membership-level-to-role mapping via a forged request granted they can trick a site administrator into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

Joomla Extension - joomlatools.com - Server-side request forgery in URL uploads in DOCman extension < 6.2.2 - The URL proxy and URL upload features were available to users below manager level and fetched arbitrary addresses, allowing server-side requests to internal or private network resources.

The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion in version up to, and including, 0.9.134. This is due to a timing side channel in the bundled RSA decryption path, insufficient validation of migration receiver backup records, and missing path validation in the cleanup_local_backup() function. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to recover an active migration receiver's RSA modulus, inject a backup record containing path traversal, and cause a later scheduled cleanup to delete an attacker-selected file writable by the web server. Exploitation requires an unexpired receiver key generated by an administrator and a subsequent manual or scheduled backup lifecycle.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could store attacker-controlled data in finding exclusion rule metadata. Another authenticated user could later open the Finding Exclusion Rules page. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who opened the page. The first user could access data and perform actions available to the later user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not escape backslashes in finding exclusion rule metadata before adding the values to a page search.
For more information see Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security) and Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

A vulnerability was found in D-Link DCS-935L 1.10.01. This affects the function loginRouter of the file web/cgi-bin/localrecording/setconf.cgi of the component Local Recording CGI. Performing a manipulation of the argument account/password results in os command injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the mc_investigation_read capability could inject arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) into Mission Control dashboard search requests. Mission Control could then run the injected SPL with elevated permissions. With this access, the user could cause Mission Control to read stored credentials and write data to indexes and lookups.
The vulnerability is possible because Mission Control does not validate reserved search filters before adding them to dashboard searches.
For more information see Overview of Mission Control in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.1/mission-control/overview-of-mission-control-in-splunk-enterprise-security) and Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.2/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

Incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs in WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4 could have caused a target's device to reveal its IP information to an attacker if an attacker sent media from an attacker-controlled URL when a crafted Click to WhatsApp ad-reply message was rendered and displayed in a message thread. This issue may have been abused in conjunction with specific spam messages.

An authenticated attacker with the Resource Administrator or Administrator role can create SNMP configuration objects through iControl SOAP resulting in privilege escalation.  Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

An authenticated attacker with the Resource Administrator or Administrator role can modify configuration objects through iControl SOAP resulting in privilege escalation.  Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

A vulnerability exists in iControl REST and the TMOS Shell (tmsh) where a highly privileged, authenticated attacker with at least the Manager role can create configuration objects that allow running arbitrary commands.

 Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

A vulnerability exists in iControl REST where a highly privileged, authenticated attacker with at least the Manager role can create configuration objects that allow running arbitrary commands.

 Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an unauthenticated user could trick an authenticated user into opening a link that the unauthenticated user creates. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the authenticated user. The commands could access data and perform actions available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the Lookup Editor does not validate lookup identifiers from URL parameters before adding them to searches.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the user by tricking them into opening a link that the attacker creates. The unauthenticated user should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Create and manage lookups in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.0/managing-security-content/create-and-manage-lookups-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_user" Splunk Enterprise Security role could run a search that causes attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) text to appear in the Search Audit dashboard. If another user who can access the dashboard selects the affected search, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled SPL commands using the permissions of the user who selects the search. The user who runs the first search could then access sensitive data and modify some data available to the user who selects the affected search.
The vulnerability is possible because the Search Audit dashboard does not safely escape logged search text before inserting it into drilldown searches.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Audit dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/audit-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in endpoint summary data. If another user who can access the Time Center dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify some data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Time Center dashboard does not safely escape endpoint summary values before inserting them into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Endpoint dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/endpoint-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, MapServer's MySQL JOIN implementation in src/mapjoin.c copies the source layer attribute selected by JOIN ... FROM into joininfo->target and inserts it into the query built by msMySQLJoinNext() without parameterization or SQL escaping. When MySQL JOIN support is enabled, an attacker who can control that source feature attribute, including through imported shapefile or DBF data or another untrusted spatial source, can inject SQL operators or expressions that change the intended JOIN predicate. This can bypass the intended key comparison and expose unrelated records from the MySQL or MariaDB JOIN table through output templates, query responses, or downstream application logic. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

A flaw was found in KubeVirt/containerized-data-importer. When a VirtualMachine with an embedded DataVolumeTemplate carrying the cdi.kubevirt.io/storage.checkStaticVolume annotation and a cross-namespace clone source is created by a tenant, the service-account clone authorization check can be bypassed, allowing a PVC from another namespace to be cloned into the tenant's namespace without the required permissions. This can result in cross-tenant data disclosure.

memtomem-stm is a short-term memory proxy gateway with proactive memory surfacing for AI agents. From 0.1.2 until 0.1.34, concurrent surfacing RPC failures can start more than one reconnect for the same dirty session because concurrent LTM recovery is not uniquely owned by a session generation. Cancellation during a post-reconnect retry can also leave the replacement transport reusable after an interrupted protocol exchange, causing session-state integrity loss or local service degradation. The duplicate-reconnect subcase was introduced in 0.1.24, while the cancellation-recovery subcase affects the broader listed range. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.34.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled certificate values. If another user who can access the Secure Sockets Layer Search dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Secure Sockets Layer Search dashboard encodes certificate values for the drilldown link but does not escape the values as SPL search literals before inserting the values into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Protocol intelligence dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/protocol-intelligence-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

wcmatch is a Python library for wildcard file-name matching. Prior to 11.2, under the default flags, matching a non-matching attacker-controlled name against an application-supplied pattern containing several star wildcards separated by literals makes the lazy .? and [^/]? segments, including _STAR and _PATH_STAR emitted by _handle_star() in wcmatch/_wcparse.py, backtrack across possible splits, so a single comparison can consume prolonged CPU time. The pattern remains a developer-controlled constant and only the name is attacker-controlled; affected paths include fnmatch.fnmatch(), glob.globmatch(), and filesystem glob scans where another user can create names, without enabling extglob or any non-default flag. This issue is fixed in 11.2.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. Prior to 4.4.3, the afpd Spotlight RPC unmarshalling loop in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c subtracts an attacker-controlled subcount from the unsigned count variable in sl_unpack_loop without verifying that subcount is not larger. An authenticated AFP client can place an excessive element count in the sl_unpack_ints, sl_unpack_uuid, sl_unpack_floats, or sl_unpack_date handler, or in a null element, so the subtraction wraps near UINT_MAX and the loop continues reading heap memory at increasing offsets up to toc_offset, which is capped at 65000. The out-of-bounds values can be stored in dalloc structures and returned in the Spotlight RPC response, disclosing heap contents. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to view an affected container could query the Representational State Transfer (REST) API for approvals to retrieve a live external prompt link belonging to another user. Using this link, the user could read the approval prompt without authentication and submit a response, potentially disrupting or altering the automated workflow governed by that approval.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API for approvals exposes the live external prompt link without verifying that the requester owns the approval.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 1.5.0 until 4.5.1, dsi_tcp_open in libatalk/dsi/dsi_tcp.c silently limits the bytes read from an unauthenticated DSI frame received on TCP/548 to server_quantum when the attacker-controlled dsi_len is larger, without rejecting the frame or draining the declared remainder. The same silent dsi_len truncation pattern exists in libatalk/dsi/dsi_stream.c. The leftover bytes remain queued on the TCP connection and the next dsi_stream_receive call interprets them as a new DSI header and payload, allowing a remote unauthenticated attacker to smuggle one or more additional attacker-controlled DSI frames into the same connection. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.1.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 8.2.0 until 8.6.5, an unauthenticated attacker can send a WMS GetLegendGraphic request with a nonempty BBOX and repeated LAYER parameters to trigger a heap buffer overflow in msWMSDispatch() in src/mapwms.cpp. The handler appends synthesized entries to cgiRequestObj.ParamNames and cgiRequestObj.ParamValues at NumParams without retaining the arrays' capacity or reallocating them, while incrementing NumParams inside the loop. Once the parser's hidden capacity is exhausted, the writes pass the heap allocation boundary. A single request can corrupt heap memory and crash the process; code execution may be possible but was not demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the HTML bookmark import action in app/Actions/ImportHtmlBookmarks.php uses the global Link::whereUrl() lookup instead of restricting duplicate detection to the importing user. An authenticated user can submit a chosen URL and distinguish the skipped response count from the queued count to learn whether any account has saved that URL, including as a PRIVATE bookmark. The oracle reveals URL existence but does not directly return the bookmark contents or owner. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with edit permission for a container or workbook task could store attacker-controlled Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) in a note. When another user with view permission for the affected container and its notes opens the affected note in Mission Control, the note could run unauthorized JavaScript code in the browser of that user, expose data available through the authenticated session, and perform actions available through the authenticated session.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not neutralize active content in all notes before Mission Control renders them.

Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in Datasolution AcyMailing SMTP Newsletter acymailing allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects AcyMailing SMTP Newsletter: from n/a through 11.1.0.

pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. From 3.48 until 3.69.1, release/skills/pmo-skill-refiner/eval-viewer/generate_review.py reads untrusted model or skill output from workspace/run*/outputs/ and embeds it with json.dumps into viewer.html inside an inline script without escaping HTML metacharacters. A crafted output can close the script element and execute JavaScript when an operator generates and opens the viewer. The maintainer also confirmed that DOM-based injection through renderGrades and renderBenchmark innerHTML survives transport-only escaping, so affected render sinks must neutralize the content. Executed script can read embedded prompts and outputs, alter the viewer DOM, or modify saved feedback. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Knit Pay Knit Pay knit-pay allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Knit Pay: from n/a through 9.6.4.0.

pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.73, release/skills/pmo-skill-refiner/eval-viewer/generate_review.py and viewer.html contain three security weaknesses in the local evaluation viewer. During workspace scanning and generation, _find_runs_recursive and build_run follow symlinks and embed_file reads their targets without confining resolved paths to the workspace, although the server do_GET path is not a traversal surface. embed_file also reads output files without a size cap or redaction, allowing secrets or personally identifiable information to be embedded in a no-auth locally served page or shareable static file. Separately, do_POST /api/feedback writes caller-supplied JSON without authentication, an Origin check, or a cross-site request forgery token, allowing a malicious page or DNS-rebound localhost target to modify feedback while the server runs. This issue is fixed in version 3.73.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user who holds a role with permission to view system settings but not assets could view asset, app, and container-label metadata in Ingestion filters.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR returns Ingestion filter metadata without applying asset authorization and tenant restrictions.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.5.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.7, tree-entry validation in src/models/GitTree.js does not reject the Windows NTFS reserved pathname alias .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION. When clone() or checkout materializes an attacker-controlled tree containing this alias on Windows using an NTFS filesystem, the alias resolves to the active .git directory and permits writes to trusted repository metadata instead of a normal worktree directory. A malicious repository or object stream can therefore poison repository configuration, hooks, refs, attributes, or other gitdir state. Strict hosting that rejects hasDotgit objects can block the crafted tree, and non-NTFS systems do not interpret the pathname as the active gitdir. isomorphic-git performs the gitdir write but does not itself execute the written hook or configuration; a later native Git or compatible-tool action, such as processing a poisoned core.fsmonitor value, can execute configured commands as the victim developer or CI identity. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.7.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker with access to an SVG upload flow can hide a script element in an internal DTD entity. NukeViet\Files\Upload::check_svg_tmpfile() loads the document without entity expansion, leaving a DOMEntityReference, and sanitize_svg_dom() inspects only element nodes, while browsers expand the entity when the stored file is served as image/svg+xml. The SVG path also returned before verify_image() and preserved the original bytes, so the hidden script reached disk unchanged. Guest comment attachments make the upload unauthenticated only when a module's comment feature is open to the All or Guest group and allowattachcomm is enabled; module administrators can also use the file manager, allowing same-origin script execution in an administrator's session. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Tribulant Software Newsletters newsletters-lite allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Newsletters: from n/a through 4.18.2.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in BdThemes Prime Slider – Addons For Elementor bdthemes-prime-slider-lite allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Prime Slider – Addons For Elementor: from n/a through 5.1.2.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From the 3.x release line until 4.6.01, an unauthenticated visitor can submit a Contact module message containing an event-handler attribute prefixed by a slash. NukeViet\Core\Request::filterTags() tokenizes attributes using only ASCII spaces, so it sees /onerror and misses the ^on denylist, while the browser treats the slash as a separator and activates onerror. The message is stored and rendered without output encoding in the administration panel, which lacks a Content Security Policy, allowing same-origin JavaScript execution when an administrator opens the message. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.01, an unauthenticated visitor can submit Contact module content containing numeric HTML entities with more than eight leading zeros in a URL-bearing attribute. NukeViet\Core\Request::unhtmlentities() does not decode that form before filterAttr() checks for a javascript: scheme, but browsers decode it when rendering the stored content. With an allowed tag such as the default iframe, the reconstructed script URL executes in the administration origin when staff view the message, permitting session-riding actions while remaining unable to read the HttpOnly session cookie directly. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. In 4.6.00, an unauthenticated attacker can rotate X-Forwarded-For because vendor/vinades/nukeviet/Core/Ips.php accepts forwarded client-IP headers without first confirming that REMOTE_ADDR is a trusted proxy. The resulting NV_CLIENT_IP keys the administrator login blocker in includes/core/admin_login.php; changing only the header value bypasses that lockout and permits effectively unlimited password guesses. The same spoofable address is also consumed by the user login blocker in modules/users/funcs/login.php, IP restrictions, bans, flood controls, and security logs, but those additional code-level effects were not dynamically demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

Key exchange without entity authentication vulnerability in Apache Tomcat allowed an unauthenticated node to join a cluster when the cluster was secured with TLS 1.3 and TLS-PSK.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: 11.0.28-11.0.29, 10.1.62, 9.0.124.



Users are recommended to switch to TLS 1.2 and TLS-PSK or upgrade to version 11.0.30, 10.1.63 or 9.0.125 (when released), which fix the issue.

AIT GUI provides a framework for building custom websites for real-time telemetry monitoring, commanding, and other mission operations. From 1.0.0 until 2.5.1, POST /tlm/query in ait/gui/__init__.py writes attacker-controlled field data to fields_in.txt, and its no-PCAP error path can abort before deleting that file. The unauthenticated POST /script/run route accepts a scriptPath that resolves outside ScriptRoot, reads the selected file, and executes it as Python. A network-reachable attacker can obtain the ordinary session cookie without credentials, combine the two routes, and execute arbitrary Python code with the AIT-GUI server process privileges. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.1.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.08 until 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker can place NukeViet's internal {@[, ]@}, [@{, and }@] sanitizer markers in an iframe srcdoc value by encoding square brackets as HTML entities. Recursive NukeViet\Core\Request::filterTags() processing decodes the characters, accepts the forged marker, and later converts it to real markup without normal tag or attribute filtering. Because an unsandboxed srcdoc iframe shares the parent origin and iframe is enabled by default through NV_ALLOWED_HTML_TAGS, stored Contact messages, comments with the editor enabled, or submitted articles can execute JavaScript with the viewer's session. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with playbook edit permission could cause later playbook conversions to include spurious branch conditions. This can prevent downstream blocks from running in affected converted playbooks.
The vulnerability is possible because the playbook converter retains branch conditions from previous conversions.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, the Comment module accepts attacker-controlled base64 content in the status_comment parameter through modules/comment/funcs/main.php; modules/comment/comment.php decodes it with nv_base64_decode() and assigns it to STATUS_COMMENT without output escaping. The required checkss token was derived from the site-wide NV_CACHE_PREFIX rather than NV_CHECK_SESSION, so a token disclosed in public comment markup could be reused across sessions in a crafted URL. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore cause decoded HTML or JavaScript to render in a victim's browser and perform phishing or same-origin actions. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, MapServer's PostgreSQL JOIN implementation in src/mappostgresql.c copies the source layer attribute selected by JOIN FROM into joininfo->from_value and embeds it without parameterization or escaping into a dynamically generated PostgreSQL query executed by PQexec(). When PostgreSQL JOIN support is enabled, an attacker who can control that source feature attribute can inject quote characters and SQL operators that alter the intended WHERE predicate. This second-order injection can cause unintended rows and JOIN attributes to be returned, potentially exposing information from unrelated PostgreSQL records. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.00, a network attacker who can alter outbound traffic to the extension store can exploit the HTTP client's disabled sslverify setting to substitute a serialized response. Extension-store handlers pass the response to unserialize() without an allowed_classes restriction, allowing an in-tree GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar gadget to write attacker-controlled content to a chosen path. When a GODADMIN opens or uses the store list, detail, install, or update functions, the substituted response can write a PHP file under the web root and execute code as the web-server user. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.00.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.2, the Spotlight RPC consumer handlers sl_rpc_fetchAttributeNamesForOIDArray, sl_rpc_storeAttributesForOIDArray, and sl_rpc_fetchAttributesForOIDArray in etc/afpd/spotlight.c dereference the first element of a decoded sl_cnids_t without checking whether the inner CNID array is empty. An authenticated AFP client, or a guest when guest AFP access is enabled, can send a crafted SPOTLIGHT_CMD_RPC whose outer CNIDS length is greater than 16 while its inner count is zero, causing sl_unpack_cnids to create an empty DALLOC_CTX and the consumer to dereference dd_talloc_array[0]. The affected afpd child crashes, normally limiting denial of service to the attacker's session, and no memory write or code execution was demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with edit permission on a workbook could configure a service-level agreement at only the workbook phase or task level. Splunk SOAR then flags the task as overdue immediately and does not display the configured deadline in the work queue. The incorrect deadline status could obscure genuine deadline breaches.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR treats an absent phase-level or task-level service-level agreement as immediately due when it compares the configured due times.
For more information see Define tasks using workbooks (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/7.0.0/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/define-tasks-using-workbooks) in the Splunk documentation.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, an unauthenticated attacker can submit the __serverInfoUpdate=1 field while controlling X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto. NukeViet\Core\Server::standardizeHost() did not validate the forwarded host against my_domains, and a trailing slash could preserve an attacker-selected port that server_info_update() used to construct a cURL request in includes/ini.php before authentication. The blind, HEAD-only request uses a fixed path, but it permits internal host and port discovery and can poison cached server_headers. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 6.0 until 8.6.5, MapServer's WMS OpenLayers output, selected by FORMAT=application/openlayers or template=openlayers, substitutes a request-derived online-resource value into a single-quoted JavaScript string in src/maptemplate.c. The prior remediation for GHSA-xqj6-vjqr-33vv used msEscapeJSonLikeString() to protect the JavaScript string but did not neutralize angle brackets, so attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Host or X-Forwarded-Proto values can still terminate the script element at the HTML parser layer. Deployments that expose attacker-controlled PATH_INFO or map= values reaching the same string are also affected. An unauthenticated attacker can cause arbitrary JavaScript to execute in a victim's browser under the MapServer origin when the victim loads the crafted output. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.
No replay or command-integrity protection. Commands lack sequence numbers, nonces, or session tokens; captured commands can be replayed, and the last command persists across sessions.

Pozeiden is a MermaidJS renderer written in Zig. Prior to 0.3.0, src/renderers/c4.zig, src/renderers/class.zig, src/renderers/er.zig, and src/renderers/requirement.zig use fixed row-layout arrays while deriving subsequent loop bounds from an untrusted diagram's actual item count, and src/renderers/state.zig indexes a fixed depth array using user-controlled nesting depth. A valid diagram with at least 193 grid items can make the row count exceed the 64-row storage, while a deeply nested state diagram can exceed the col_count depth storage through the public pozeiden.render() path. Safe CLI and ReleaseSafe builds abort the rendering process, enabling reliable denial of service in applications that render untrusted diagrams. ReleaseSmall WASM builds with safety checks disabled instead perform out-of-bounds stack reads or writes, creating a memory-safety violation. This issue is fixed in version 0.3.0.

The affected products have an unauthenticated command injection, which may allow an in-range BLE device to gain access to write to the control interface and influence braking with no authentication or pairing.

pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.73, core/hooks/block-fragile-refs.sh and core/hooks/block-gh-path-leak.sh source co-shipped awk primitives from core/hooks/lib/ and degrade when a required primitive is absent. In a partial or corrupted deployment, block-gh-path-leak.sh skips its entire path-leak check, while block-fragile-refs.sh skips only the positional-issue-reference detector and continues running its other detectors. Both hooks operate in a warning posture, so the impact is a skipped warning rather than bypass of an enforcing control, with no established exfiltration or code-execution primitive. This issue is fixed in version 3.73.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, an unauthenticated reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in OGC API Features collection-items HTML output allows crafted offset or limit query parameter values from raw CGI request handling in src/mapogcapi.cpp to reach template.params.offset or template.params.limit. share/ogcapi/templates/html-bootstrap/collection-items.html inserts those values without quoting or escaping into a script element. A victim who follows a crafted request can have the script element terminated by attacker-controlled markup, causing arbitrary JavaScript to execute under the MapServer origin and enabling access to browser-session data, actions as the victim, and content manipulation. This issue is fixed in 8.6.5.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding.

The encoder routes any value with abs >= 2**31 to i2osp without validating that it is an integer. A string in exponent notation such as "1e8000" passes that threshold. Math::BigInt expands it to an 8001-digit integer, and i2osp's per-octet conversion loop is quadratic in that size.

An attacker who controls encoded INTEGER values can exhaust CPU with a short exponent-notation string.

A heap-based buffer overflow was found in Corosync's Totem SRP membership commit token handling. The sanity check for memb_commit_token messages validates only minimum length and address-entry counts, not an upper bound against the fixed commit_token_storage buffer. A network-adjacent attacker who can deliver a crafted oversized commit token to a node in the GATHER membership state may overflow the heap-allocated totemsrp instance, leading to memory corruption and denial of service.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via zero-length BIT STRING content.

A BIT STRING with zero content octets passes -1 to substr as the length. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the decoded value is nearly all of the input that follows the element. In the constructed form each zero-length segment copies the rest of the input again, so memory grows with the square of the input size.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a short constructed BIT STRING. The resulting value also contains bytes from adjacent input.

LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.5.9, the authenticated GET /api/v2/lists/{list}/links endpoint in app/Http/Controllers/API/ListLinksController.php authorizes access only to the parent list and then returns its links without applying visibleForUser(). Because another user's INTERNAL or PUBLIC list may legitimately contain PRIVATE links, a normal authenticated user who may view the list can also receive those private link records, including their URLs, titles, descriptions, icons, and timestamps. Equivalent web, tag, notes, and feed handlers apply the per-link visibility scope, so this API handler is the affected exception. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.9.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding.

Any constructed-form string element causes the decoder to recurse on the element's contents. The BER encoding controls nesting depth at four bytes per level, with no bound checked. Perl recursion is heap-allocated, so the process grows without a stack crash.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a small deeply nested constructed string.

A flaw was found in NetworkManager-iodine, the iodine VPN plugin for NetworkManager. A local unprivileged user can exploit a vulnerability in how the 'nameserver' setting is processed when establishing an iodine VPN connection. By embedding shell metacharacters (special characters that can execute commands) in the 'nameserver' value, an attacker can inject and execute arbitrary commands. These commands run with root privileges before the application drops its elevated permissions, leading to local privilege escalation.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unbounded arc length in OBJECT IDENTIFIER decoding and encoding.

The content of an OBJECT IDENTIFIER or RELATIVE-OID element is passed to unpack "w*" on decode, and the arcs of an OID string to pack "w*" on encode. Perl converts each arc to or from its decimal string in time quadratic in the arc's length, and nothing limits that length.

An attacker who controls the decoded data, or an OID string passed to encode, can exhaust CPU with a single oversized arc.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.2, sl_createCNIDArray in etc/afpd/spotlight.c assumes every element of kMDQueryItemArray points to an eight-byte uint64_t and copies sizeof(uint64_t) bytes from the indexed p->dd_talloc_array element without validating the element's talloc type or allocation size. An authenticated AFP client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can use FPSpotlightRPC to supply a mixed-type sl_array_t containing a shorter boolean, nil, or string element, and an unauthenticated client can reach the same path when the optional guest UAM and a guest-accessible volume are enabled. The resulting eight-byte read extends beyond the shorter element's heap allocation and supplies an internal CNID filter; no confidentiality channel, write primitive, or code execution was demonstrated, while a production crash would require additional heap placement conditions. The container-type validation added for CVE-2023-42464 does not validate each element inside an accepted sl_array_t and therefore does not resolve this issue. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 1.5.0 until 4.5.1, dsi_stream_receive in libatalk/dsi/dsi_stream.c independently clamps dsi_doff and dsi_len for DSIWrite requests without enforcing that the data offset is no greater than the declared frame length. An authenticated AFP client can send dsi_doff greater than dsi_len, causing the receiver to consume bytes from a queued subsequent frame before libatalk/dsi/dsi_write.c detects the inconsistency. The irreversible stream desynchronization lets the attacker control the next parsed DSI header and payload and corrupts protocol framing for the connection. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.1.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read and asn_get.

The length an element declares in its BER header is passed to sysread as the read size. Perl grows the target buffer to that size before reading, so memory is allocated from the declared length, not from the data received. A 6-byte header can declare a length of up to 4GB.

A single header makes the reading process allocate the declared size. Where the allocation fails, perl exits with "Out of memory", which eval cannot catch.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. Prior to 4.4.3, the afpd Spotlight RPC string unmarshalling path in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c uses sl_unpack_cpx to calculate slen from qlen and the attacker-controlled used_in_last_block value without preventing a negative result. An authenticated AFP client can send a complex string or UTF-16 string element that makes slen negative, and the implicit conversion to size_t causes dalloc_strndup or convert_string_allocate to read beyond the heap buffer. The out-of-bounds read can expose heap data through the RPC response or crash the worker process. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.
libumqtt is vulnerable to an integer underflow which may allow a remote attacker to cause a denial of service, memory corruption, or information disclosure.
The affected products use an unprotected firmware-update channel, which may allow for unauthorized firmware modification.

svglib reads SVG files and converts them to other formats. Prior to 2.3.1, the svg2rlg() renderer recursively expands nested SVG <use> references by deep-copying each referenced subtree; SvgRenderer.renderUse() in src/svglib/svglib.py calls xlink_href_target(), which rejects direct cycles but permits acyclic reference graphs with repeated fan-out. A small attacker-controlled SVG can therefore trigger exponentially increasing node expansion, consuming excessive CPU and memory in any application that renders it without a non-default option; HTML-to-PDF workflows using xhtml2pdf can reach the same renderer when an embedded data:image/svg+xml image in an HTML img element is passed to pisa.CreatePDF(). This issue is fixed in 2.3.1.

Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache Tomcat in the CGI Servlet when handling POST bodies can result in a DoS for some inputs.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.50.0, a BASIC application user, or an unauthenticated visitor to a public write form, can store markup in a shared external datasource that a builder or administrator later evaluates in any Handlebars binding Preview that surfaces the value, including the Data-section Formula column editor or any binding drawer. jsonFormatter.format() in packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts leaves raw strings and object keys unescaped, while packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte inserts the formatted result as raw HTML. The Handlebars SafeString path preserves the attacker-controlled value, and the Builder origin lacks a Content-Security-Policy that would block the resulting script. This permits stored script execution in the higher-privileged builder or administrator session rather than the writer's own role, allowing privileged Builder API actions and workspace data access. This issue is fixed in versions 3.50.0 and 4.0.0.

Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache Tomcat during HTTP upgrade in some circumstances lead to possible DoS.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.41 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.61 through 8.5.100. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

The GiveWP – Donation Plugin and Fundraising Platform plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to donor account account takeover in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0. This is due to the plugin not properly validating a donor's identity prior to updating the password of a linked WordPress account. The donation receipt processes an attacker-controlled first name through the V3 template engine and then reprocesses the result through the legacy `{meta_donor_*}` engine, which can disclose the donor's email-access bearer token. The donor-dashboard password endpoint accepts that token by itself and calls `wp_set_password()` for the WordPress user linked to the donor. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to reset the password of any WordPress account linked to a GiveWP donor record and gain access to that account. If the linked account is an administrator, the attacker can achieve full site compromise and remote code execution through standard administrator functionality. A published GiveWP form with a usable gateway, enabled donor email access (enabled by default), knowledge of the donor email address, and an account already linked to the targeted donor record are required. NOTE: This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-82676 to satisfy the administrator donor pre-requisite for a targeted administrator user attack.
vp: givewp – donation plugin and fundraising platform

cves.d:
Execution After Redirect (EAR) vulnerability in Apache Tomcat in RedirectValve affecting flags [F], [G] and [R].



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M18 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.20 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.87 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: 8.5.100. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62, 9.0.124, which fixes the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

Pydici through 2026.11.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by storing HTML in contact names rendered unescaped in the contact detail mermaid diagram. Attackers with contact edit permission can store malicious markup that Contact.relationData() interpolates and contact_detail.html renders with the safe filter, executing script in victims' sessions.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic bigint loop in os2ip.

Every INTEGER or ENUMERATED longer than four content octets reaches os2ip, which iterates over each content octet with $result = ($result * 256) + $octet. Each multiplication operates on a bigint that grows by one octet per step, so decoding an n-octet value takes O(n^2) bigint work. Nothing limits content length before this loop runs.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a single oversized INTEGER or ENUMERATED value.

Kartones flask-calendar before commit bfde72e contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because task_details_for_markup returns unescaped content rendered with the |safe filter. Authenticated shared calendar members can store script in task details that executes for other members, letting attackers read and modify their private calendars.

The fix for CVE-2026-25854 was incomplete.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.19 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.53 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.116 through 9.0.123.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv.

asn_recv peeks the socket in a loop, doubling the buffer size on each pass until a tag and length can be decoded. An inverted boolean guard ($tb || rather than $tb &&) prevents the need-more-data exit from firing once a tag byte has been decoded. When asn_decode_length returns no value because the length is absent or incomplete, no exit fires for that case either. MSG_PEEK leaves socket data unconsumed, so each re-peek returns at once while the buffer size doubles.

A single truncated BER header sent to a process calling asn_recv doubles the peek buffer until memory is exhausted. Perl's realloc failure is fatal and not catchable with eval.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.00 until 4.5.13 and 4.6.02, an unauthenticated attacker can place a multiply encoded value in the news module search q parameter. $nv_Request->get_title() decodes and sanitizes the input once, but modules/news/funcs/search.php subsequently applies urldecode() after sanitization. The resulting raw keyword reaches the {KEY} search-input attribute through search_theme() and the no-results element through search_result_theme() in the default and mobile themes, permitting attribute or tag injection and same-origin JavaScript execution when a victim opens the crafted search URL. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.13 and 4.6.02.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unchecked exponent length in binary REAL decoding.

Binary REAL decoding never bounds-checks the exponent length against the available content. For a minimal one-byte binary REAL, the exponent byte is read from outside the element, making the mantissa length -1. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the mantissa is nearly all of the input that follows the element. The long-form exponent path also omits the extra length octet when sizing the mantissa.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a list of such values, as each mantissa loop iterates over the remaining input. The decoded values are also computed from bytes outside each element.

Missing release of resource after effective lifetime vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's HTTP/2 initial connection handling leads to DoS.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.20 through 9.0.123.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker who can reach an image-upload flow can upload a valid image with appended PHP short-tag code and a double-extension filename. NukeViet\Files\Upload::save_file() relied on verify_image(), which missed the <? short-open tag, while filename handling preserved embedded dots, validation inspected only the final extension, and an .htaccess rule blocked PHP extensions only at the end of the URI. On Apache mod_php systems configured with short_open_tag and a PHP extension handler, the stored polyglot can execute as PHP and run operating-system commands as the web-server user; PHP-FPM, nginx, and end-anchored handler configurations are not exposed to the execution step. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory in the file access checks in Amazon awslabs.document-loader-mcp-server 1.0.10 through 1.0.20 might allow a context-dependent actor, via crafted document content processed by an MCP client, to read files outside the intended base directory and, in 1.0.12 through 1.0.20, to write PNG slide images outside it. This occurs when DOCUMENT_BASE_DIR is not set or is empty and the CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS or PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST environment variable is present. Versions before 1.0.10 do not restrict file access to a base directory.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 1.0.21 or later. Users who cannot upgrade immediately can set DOCUMENT_BASE_DIR to the directory that holds their documents. Do not set it to /, which removes the restriction.

Missing release of memory after effective lifetime vulnerability in Apache Tomcat via WebSocket.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.22 through 9.0.123



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.43 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.0.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

Authorization bypass via a user-controlled key in XOneManager 3.8.3.0. The 'ConvertBDToProject' operation selects the database based on 'databasename' without verifying the user’s permissions on it. An authenticated user can link a project to a database outside their scope and identify existing databases based on API responses.

The WPO365 | SEAMLESS WORDPRESS + MICROSOFT INTEGRATION (WPO365 | LOGIN) WordPress plugin before 45.4 does not ensure the signature validated on a SAML response covers the element the user identity is read from, allowing unauthenticated attackers to forge a response via signature wrapping and log in as any user, including administrators, when they can supply a single artifact signed by the configured identity provider.
vp: wpo365 | seamless wordpress + microsoft integration (wpo365 | login)

cves.d: The SAML SSO Login  WordPress plugin through 1.5.2 does not verify that the SAML assertion whose signature it validates is the same assertion it reads the user identity from, allowing unauthenticated attackers who hold a validly signed assertion for any identity to authenticate as any existing user, including an administrator, through XML signature wrapping.

When a scheduled export is copied, the permissions of the original export's owner are used when running the export. This allows users to create exports with data they usually shouldn't be able to see, but only within events they already have permissions to.

The AppPresser  WordPress plugin before 5.0.0 does not properly escape the contents of its debug log when displaying it in the admin dashboard, and decodes escape sequences after sanitising input, allowing unauthenticated users to perform Stored XSS attacks against administrators when debug logging is enabled.

Improper cleanup on thrown exception vulnerability in Apache Tomcat meant that an HTTP 200 response was sent rather than an HTTP 500 response after a AuthException was thrown during Jakarta Authentication secureResponse().



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.0.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

When a ticket holder opens the ticket page of a ticket that is an add-on (possible since 2026.9) the HTML content of the page contains the secret link to the parent product, creating a potential data leak. Under different specific conditions, when a ticket contains user-uploaded files in response to a question, the page can even contain the secret link to the entire order.

The Lightbox with PhotoSwipe WordPress plugin before 5.19.0 does not escape image link URLs before outputting them in the attributes of the lightbox share menu, allowing unauthenticated users to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks via comments when the PhotoSwipe 4 frontend is used.

The User Registration Aide WordPress plugin through 1.5.3.8 does not verify the current password or a reset token before changing a user's password, allowing unauthenticated attackers who know a user's username and email address to change the password of any account, including administrators, and take it over.

A legacy code path allowed users to craft requests to a ticket shop that bypass some validation steps for the selected products. In consequence, this could lead to an attacker purchasing products that are in fact sold out.

Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat could occur during a request dispatch if the request depended on a security-role-ref provided by the dispatch target.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fixes the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.00 until 4.6.01, an authenticated settings-module administrator can upload a PKCS#12 S/MIME certificate whose X.509 Subject CN contains path separators and traversal components. The smimeadd handler in admin/settings/smtp.php applies only an at-sign replacement before using the CN in .key, .crt, and .pem paths beneath data/certs. Traversal can select attacker-chosen paths outside data/certs, but writes remain constrained to already-existing writable directories and the permitted extensions. Within that constraint, attacker-controlled PEM data can overwrite certificate assets, including a DKIM private key; when the curl.cainfo PHP directive is empty, the attacker can also replace cacert.pem and undermine outbound TLS verification. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

Our payment integration with Stripe did not properly validate payment status responses. An attacker could use a successful payment status response from one payment and supply it to the system for a different payment, gaining access to multiple valid tickets with only one payment. However, the attack requires knowledge of a valid charge ID from the same event which we believe is usually not exposed to users.




To simplify attack surface, the fix removes support for incoming webhooks regarding payments created through Stripe's old "source" API. pretix stopped creating payments using this API in 2024.1 for most payment methods and in 2024.9 for all payment methods.

When configuring a device to use the security profile "pretixSCAN (kiosk mode, no order sync, no search)", the API search endpoint introduced in pretix 4.12 was not blocked correctly. This theoretically allows these devices to perform searches for orders even if that was not intended. If the device is in kiosk mode, the search button will still be hidden from users.

Reliance on obfuscation or encryption of Security-Relevant inputs without integrity checking, Improper validation of integrity check value, Cleartext transmission of sensitive information vulnerability in the EncryptInterceptor of Apache Tomcat.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.13 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.38 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.100 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124 and switch to TLS-PSK to encrypt cluster communication, which fixes the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. In 4.6.00, an unauthenticated attacker can place the configured domain in X-Forwarded-Host while choosing a different destination in the ordinary Host header. The earlier fix validates only the forwarded value in includes/mainfile.php, while set_ini_file() in includes/ini.php constructs an outbound cURL request from the separately retained NV_SERVER_NAME before the ordinary host is rejected. Redirect following can carry the blind request to an attacker-selected private host, port, and path and invoke internal HTTP endpoints. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

Joomla Extension - joomlatools.com - Local file read through remote document links in DOCman extension < 6.2.2 - Remote document links accepted the file:// scheme, allowing users with permission to create or edit documents to download arbitrary local files from the server, such as the Joomla configuration file.

Net::DNS uses a 16-bit query ID to match responses to the corresponding requests.  In versions up to and including 1.57, the ID is obtained from Perl's built-in rand() function.  An attacker that can observe the sequence of query IDs is able to expose the internal state of the PNRG and hence predict query IDs before they are transmitted.  The victim Net::DNS instance is then exposed to forged responses injected by the attacker.  Note that the deduplication cache in 1.57 has no impact on the feasibility of this attack.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management product of Oracle Hyperion (component: Reconciliation Manage).   The supported version that is affected is 11.2.26.0.000. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 3.7 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N).

Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix_live_view allows an authenticated user to mount a router-mounted LiveView without the on_mount hooks of its live_session via a phx_join message that carries neither a "url" nor a "redirect" key.

The catch-all clause of the private Phoenix.LiveView.Channel.authorize_session/3 in lib/phoenix_live_view/channel.ex accepts a join without a URL for any session, including a root LiveView mounted at the router. The channel then mounts the LiveView with no route, and only a route adds the live_session hooks to the mount lifecycle. Checks that those hooks perform on the connected mount do not run, and event checks that they attach through attach_hook/4 are never attached. The attacker needs a valid session token for the LiveView, which only the HTTP render issues, after the hooks pass there. on_mount hooks declared in the LiveView module still run.

This issue affects phoenix_live_view: from 0.16.0 before 1.0.20, from 1.1.0-rc.0 before 1.1.34, and from 1.2.0-rc.0 before 1.2.14.

In `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2` versions `<= 2.0.0-rc8` (and the deprecated v1 module paths `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11 <= 1.6.8`, `github.com/ThalesGroup/crypto11 <= 1.7.0-rc1` and `github.com/ThalesIgnite/crypto11 <= 1.2.5`), the `cipher.AEAD` returned by `SecretKey.NewGCM()` passes whatever nonce it is given straight to `CK_GCM_PARAMS` without checking its length against `NonceSize()`, and accepts an empty nonce. On a token that accepts a zero-length GCM IV — SoftHSM2 does — every `Seal` with an empty nonce encrypts under the same IV, reusing the keystream and exposing the GHASH authentication key, which allows forgeries. Separately, `Config.UseGCMIVFromHSM` sends a NULL IV with length zero to the token unless `GCMIVFromHSMControl.SupplyIvForHSMGCMEncrypt` is also set, so the token has nowhere to write the IV it generates: a `Seal` with a non-empty nonce panics after the plaintext has already been encrypted, and a `Seal` with an empty nonce returns ciphertext under an empty IV without error. On the v1 line HSM-IV mode additionally never copies the token-generated IV back to the caller, so the caller keeps its own nonce while the data was encrypted under another one.

The IPv6 Neighbor Discovery code in subsys/net/ip/ipv6_nbr.c flushes a neighbour's queued packets at the end of handle_ra_input(). The Source Link-Layer Address Option (SLLAO) is optional in a Router Advertisement; when it is absent, handle_ra_input() still obtains (or creates) a neighbour cache entry for the RA source via net_ipv6_nbr_add() with a NULL link-layer address, so the entry stays in NET_IPV6_NBR_STATE_INCOMPLETE with nbr->idx == NET_NBR_LLADDR_UNKNOWN. The pending-packet drain loop was entered unconditionally for that unresolved entry.

Each net_send_data() in the drain loop runs synchronously into net_ipv6_prepare_for_send(), which finds the neighbour still unresolved and hands the packet to net_ipv6_send_ns(), which puts it straight back onto the same pending_queue. The loop therefore never sees an empty queue. With a single queued packet it transmits a fresh Neighbor Solicitation on every iteration; with two or more queued packets it rotates the queue with no allocation and no transmission at all. The loop runs in the network RX thread with the global IPv6 neighbour mutex held.

An unauthenticated attacker on the same link can trigger this deterministically: advertise itself as a router, induce the victim to queue off-link traffic toward that router (for example by sending echo requests with an off-link source address) while leaving the solicitation unanswered, then send a second Router Advertisement without an SLLAO option. Spoofing an SLLAO-less RA from the legitimate router's link-local address has the same effect whenever traffic is queued for it. Router Advertisements are processed with no authentication whenever CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ND is enabled, which is the default for IPv6-capable builds.

The result is a permanent denial of service: the RX thread spins forever holding the neighbour lock, so all IPv6 transmission and every other user of the neighbour cache blocks, and the Neighbor Advertisement that would resolve the entry can no longer be processed. The ipv6_ns_reply_timer work item that would normally drop the pending packets also blocks on the same mutex. In the single-packet variant the loop additionally floods the link with Neighbor Solicitations. The fix restricts the flush to resolved entries (nbr->idx != NET_NBR_LLADDR_UNKNOWN), leaving the packets queued for the NS reply timeout. There is no memory-safety impact.

@fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards an incoming HTTP request to an upstream server. In versions before 12.9.1, when the plugin forwards a request whose body is not written to the upstream connection, such as a GET, HEAD, or TRACE request that carried a body, or a request with a falsy JSON body, it still forwards the client's Content-Length header while sending no body. The upstream server then treats the bytes of the following request as the unfinished body, which an attacker can use to desynchronize the connection and smuggle a request. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.9.1, and users should upgrade to 12.9.1 or later.

net_if_ipv4_addr_rm() and net_if_ipv6_addr_rm() in subsys/net/ip/net_if.c unconditionally called net_if_addr_unref() on the target address. When an earlier removal could not complete because another subsystem still held a reference (the TCP stack takes one on the local address of every connection, in tcp_conn_new() and on connect()), the address is left in place with is_added cleared and is_used still set. A second removal of such an address decremented the reference count again, consuming a reference owned by that other holder. When it was the last one, the address slot was released, its NET_EVENT_IPV*_ADDR_DEL event fired, and the slot became reusable while the holder still believed it owned a reference.

Every address lookup helper matches on is_used and not on is_added, so a half-removed address stays visible to the rest of the stack and repeat removals are readily reachable from remote input. Under IPv6 SLAAC, an on-link node that sends a Router Advertisement with a short valid lifetime causes the address to expire into the deferred state; a refreshing Router Advertisement is handled by net_if_ipv6_addr_update_lifetime(), which re-arms the lifetime timer without restoring the reference, so the next expiry performs the second, reference-stealing removal. With CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ACD and DHCPv4, repeated spoofed ARP conflicts for the device's lease drive dhcpv4_acd_event_handler() into calling net_if_ipv4_addr_rm() more than once on the same address. Where CONFIG_USERSPACE is enabled, the net_if_ipv4_addr_rm_by_index() and net_if_ipv6_addr_rm_by_index() system calls let an unprivileged user-mode thread trigger the same kernel-side release deterministically.

The impact is loss of a configured IP address while connections are still using it, and a corrupted reference count that propagates: the slot can be handed to a newly added address, and when the stale holder later tears down, net_if_addr_unref() resolves the address by value and drops the new incarnation's only reference, removing a live address a second time. The affected objects are static array slots and the counter is never decremented below zero, so there is no memory corruption or information disclosure; the consequence is denial of service against the device's network connectivity, repeatable at the attacker's pace.

The fix resolves the address before touching the reference count and returns false without calling net_if_addr_unref() when the address is already marked as removed, so the public removal API can no longer consume a reference it does not own.

The SMSC911x/LAN9220 Ethernet driver stages every outgoing frame in a fixed-size static buffer before pushing it to the controller FIFO. eth_tx() in drivers/ethernet/eth_smsc911x.c took the frame length from net_pkt_get_len(pkt) and passed it directly to net_pkt_read(pkt, tx_buf, total_len), with no comparison against the size of tx_buf (NET_ETH_MAX_FRAME_SIZE). net_pkt_read() takes no destination size and only fails when the packet is shorter than the requested length, so any packet longer than the staging buffer was copied past its end.

Nothing between the IP layer and the driver bounds the frame to what the link can carry: ethernet_send() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c performs no length check, and the IPv6 output path only compares the packet against the interface MTU when CONFIG_NET_IPV6_FRAGMENT is enabled (it is disabled by default). The size the stack will build is therefore governed by the interface MTU, and that MTU is remotely settable: handle_ra_input() in subsys/net/ip/ipv6_nbr.c honours the MTU option of any Router Advertisement with a value up to 0xffff, gated only by the standard hop-limit-255 and link-local-source checks. An unauthenticated attacker on the same link can raise the MTU and then have the device emit a single frame of several kilobytes, for example as a TCP segment from any service that returns more than ~1.5 KB or as an oversized UDP datagram.

The result is an out-of-bounds write into .bss immediately after tx_buf, with the overrun length and much of its content derived from the transmitted frame. Consequences range from corruption of adjacent kernel data and a crash to potential control-flow influence where the clobbered globals hold pointers; the practical overrun size is bounded by the network buffer pool rather than by the advertised MTU. The fix rejects frames larger than NET_ETH_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with -EMSGSIZE before any TX_DATA_PORT write, so the controller FIFO is also not left holding a command word without its payload.
